extracted.intended_audience: inventors, product designers, businesses and IP attorneys assessing design patent infringement risk
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing whether an accused product design infringes a U.S. design patent using the Federal Circuit's Egyptian Goddess/ordinary observer framework, with emphasis on comparing accused and claimed designs in the context of prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinary observer test
rubrics_metrics.description: The ordinary observer test requires one to view the differences between the accused design and the patented design in the context of the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether an ordinary observer, familiar with the prior art, would be deceived into believing the accused design is the same as the patented design. The court focuses on whether the overall visual impression to such an observer suggests deceptive similarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art as contextual baseline
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art in the context of design patents includes designs and other published documents made publicly available prior to the filing date of a design patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prior art designs/publications to determine which aspects of the claimed design are novel or conspicuous; prior art can draw the observer's attention away from or toward certain features when comparing designs. Practical example: the Nailco and Falley buffers were considered as prior art in Egyptian Goddess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observer familiar with the prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: In applying the ordinary observer test a court should view the two designs through the eyes of an observer familiar with the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the hypothetical 'ordinary observer' as someone who knows the existing design landscape for the product type — not a layperson seeing the design in a vacuum. This affects which differences are noticed and deemed important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salience of novel/conspicuous features
rubrics_metrics.description: If the accused design has copied a novel feature of the claimed design that departs conspicuously from the prior art, the accused design is naturally more likely to be regarded as deceptively similar to the claimed design, and thus, infringing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify features of the claimed design that are departures from the prior art; if the accused design replicates those conspicuous departures, infringement is more likely. This is the rationale given in Egyptian Goddess for focusing on differences from prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance of small differences when close to prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: When the claimed design is close to the prior art designs, small differences between the accused design and the claimed design are likely to be important to the eye of the hypothetical ordinary observer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the patented design largely tracks prior art, even minor variations may be determinative and can lead to a finding of non-infringement if they distinguish the designs to the ordinary observer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic overall-appearance evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the effect of different features upon the appearance of the design as a whole, when said design is viewed in context with the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts consider the cumulative visual effect rather than isolated elements. Example from Egyptian Goddess: a fourth side with a pad versus a fourth side without a pad altered the overall appearance sufficiently to support non-infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial/deceptive similarity standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The inquiry is whether the accused design is 'substantially the same' or 'deceptively similar' to the claimed design to the ordinary observer familiar with the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame infringement questions in terms of substantial or deceptive similarity rather than mechanical element-by-element matching; consider whether the accused design would deceive an ordinary observer into believing it is the patented design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative method: side-by-side analysis with prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts perform side-by-side comparisons of the patented design, the accused design, and relevant prior art designs to determine infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use visual juxtaposition of the three items (patented design, accused product, and prior art examples) to see which features stand out and how they influence the overall impression. The Egyptian Goddess opinion itself compared the '389 patent, the accused buffer, and two prior art buffers (Nailco and Falley).
